messages:
alex: ran an Nsight Systems capture on the repro workload, attaching a short clip of the timeline. seeing repeated 1-3ms gaps between kernel launch and actual GPU work on stream 2

sanjay: can you paste the nsys command you used? curious if sampling affected it

alex: command below — lightweight capture, cuda+osrt, CPU stack sampling enabled:
```
nsys profile --trace=cuda,osrt --sample=cuda,os --sample-interval=1000000 --output=perf_launch_spike %PID_OR_CMD%
```

olivia: timeline snapshot: kernels on stream 2 start, then ~2ms host-side delay, then device kernels run. memcpy's on stream 1 continue overlapping. looks like host thread requeueing? :thinking_face: 

alex: exact sequence I see: host launches kernel (cudaLaunchKernel), returns, then ~1.5–2.8ms CPU time passes before actual GPU work shows up. nvprof counters show no lost device-side queueing. CPU stacks during the gap point to our batcher thread waiting on futex + heavy memcpy progress callbacks.

marcus: could be scheduler preemption on the batcher thread. what's the CPU runqueue at that time? did you collect perf sched or /proc/softirqs?

alex: captured perf sched slices via sampling. stack shows `batcher::flush()` -> `kvcache::prefetch_cb()` -> `memcpy_async` callback where it yields to epoll_wait. traces also show a spike in `hostSpin` CPU usage right before the gap.

sanjay: timeline screenshot: https://redwood/prof/2288001111/clip (inline). see dense kernel bursts, then one gap cluster aligned to hostSpin spikes.

olivia: hypothesis: our prefetch/memcpy completion handler runs on the same CPU core as the batcher, and the kernel launch path depends on that callback to update flogging state. if the callback blocks (or gets preempted) the kernel command buffer flush gets delayed.

alex: to probe, I forced the memcpy callbacks onto a dedicated thread (pthread_affinity_set) and reran. gap reduced to ~100-300us and overall p99 tokens improved ~12%.

perf-bot: auto-report: p99 token latency decreased from 52.3ms to 45.9ms on the experiment run. CPU scheduling preemption events decreased by ~60%.

marcus: nice. do we have a safe rollout? olive, any changes needed to the batcher API?

olivia: minimal change: move completion processing into a small threadpool and only signal batcher via lock-free queue. i'll draft a patch. also add a runtime config to pin callback threads to spare cores on Dedicated.

sanjay: also flag: kernel launch latency spikes correlate with a specific CUDA driver version on one test rig (525.x). other rigs with 520.x don't show the same amplitude. could be driver scheduling interplay. we should test across driver matrix.

alex: agreed. i'll add driver version to our perf CI trace harness and stash an nsys capture per driver.

olivia: small repro steps for the patch test:
1) enable callback-threadpool via env REDWOOD_PREFETCH_CB_THREADS=2
2) run loadrunner with batch size 8, seq len 1024
3) collect `nsys profile` with `--sample=cuda,os`

alex: one more oddity: CPU stack samples during gaps show frequent `sys_nanosleep` entries in some traces. might be our exponential backoff kicking in erroneously on fallback path. watch out.

marcus: ok scope: 1) land callback threadpool + config, 2) add driver variant CI tests, 3) add detection alert in Console if p99 launch gap > 1ms and hostSpin > 10% during window. I'll open a ticket.

olivia: opening PR and will tag you all. tl;dr: nsight timeline pointed at host-side callback preemption as primary culprit, workaround is moving callback work off the batcher thread and optional core pinning.

alex: thanks — saved a lot of time vs chasing device kernels. good catch everyone. :rocket:
